final_candidates.decision_summary: E509 is in the C-terminal head-domain region proposed to contribute to the m102.4 footprint. Neutralizing the acidic side chain may weaken antibody recognition while avoiding a gross structural change.

N408Q is a conservative polar substitution in a predicted neutralization-sensitive surface region. It may alter antibody contacts or local glycosylation-associated recognition while preserving protein folding.

N411D introduces a negative charge near the proposed epitope rim and could disrupt antibody electrostatic complementarity. Its distance from the principal ephrin-binding pocket makes preservation of receptor engagement plausible.

stop_reason.detail: Further LLM-only self-iteration would not add independent evidence and is unlikely to improve the Top-3.

history.rationale: Amide-to-amide change in a surface-exposed C-terminal head loop near the presumed m102.4/receptor interface may weaken antibody H-bonding with low structural cost. Chosen to avoid bulky or hydrophobic disruption of the ephrin-binding pocket.

Residue verified (position 408 = N in 'IYDSLGQP...NWRNNTV' region); N-linked glycosylation site changes in the m102.4 epitope face are a classic escape strategy and conservative substitution preserves folding.

Introducing a negative charge at Asn411 could electrostatically disfavor m102.4-class binding while remaining soluble and surface-compatible. Risk to ephrin binding is moderated because it is adjacent to rather than inside the deepest receptor-contact residues.
Position 411 verified as N; charge introduction at the epitope rim likely disrupts antibody contact while being distant from the ephrin-B2/B3 binding pocket.
Conservative Arg-to-Lys retains positive charge but changes side-chain reach and antibody contact geometry. Likely lower escape magnitude but higher viability/receptor-binding preservation.
Position 410 verified as R; conservative basic-to-basic swap modestly perturbs antibody electrostatics while minimizing structural disruption.

Removing only the Tyr hydroxyl can erase a specific antibody hydrogen bond while preserving aromatic packing. Phenylalanine is a comparatively safe substitution for maintaining local fold and receptor surface.
Position 239 verified as Y; conservative aromatic swap at the receptor-proximal region may subtly perturb antibody docking but carries risk of affecting ephrin binding, so keep mid-rank.

Carboxylate-to-amide at a late head-domain surface residue may alter m102.4 electrostatic recognition without large hydrophobic perturbation. Position is near the C-terminal antigenic region but not an obvious core ephrin contact.

Position 509 verified as E ('LIYDTGDNVIR...IYE' region near C-terminus, '...IWCISLVEIYDTG' — position 509 E in '...LV E IY' tail); the C-terminal head domain near residue 507-511 lies in the reported m102.4 footprint, so a charge-neutralizing swap is a plausible escape mutation.

Neutralizing an acidic surface residue can reduce antibody affinity through charge/shape complementarity loss. Asp-to-Asn is small and polar, favoring protein stability and retained receptor engagement.
Without structural confirmation, residue 445 is uncertain to be surface-exposed in the epitope; low-confidence candidate dropped to focus the pool.

rejection.reason: Without structural confirmation, residue 445 is uncertain to be surface-exposed in the epitope; low-confidence candidate dropped to focus the pool.

history.rationale: Glycine adds local flexibility at an exposed loop position that may remodel an antibody epitope. Low-complexity substitution reduces chance of destabilization but gives more modest expected escape.
Glycine introduction risks local flexibility/folding issues with weak rationale for epitope contact; dropped.

history.rationale: Alanine removes a long charged side chain from a surface patch, potentially reducing ionic antibody contacts. It may also slightly reduce solubility of that patch, so confidence is lower.
Position uncertain to contact m102.4 and alanine scan effects unpredictable without data; dropped.

history.rationale: Late-sequence acidic residue neutralization could perturb C-terminal epitope recognition while keeping a polar amide side chain. Distal location suggests limited direct effect on ephrin-B2/B3 binding.
Position 515 verified as D ('...IYDTGDNV'); near the C-terminal epitope region, charge removal could escape antibody binding.

A small polar-to-hydrophobic switch near a loop around residues 401-412 may reduce antibody binding through desolvation effects. This carries higher receptor-interface risk, so it is ranked cautiously in the initial pool.
